name: New Web App
description: Dark Factory playbook for scaffolding a brand-new web application from scratch: triage the intake, plan the architecture, build it, and gate only on the final merge review.

epicPlaybook.promptOverride: Scaffold the new web application per the approved plan. Before transitioning to execution-complete, run the project's full test suite and its linter/typecheck (e.g. `npm test` and `npm run typecheck` / `npm run lint`). Do NOT transition to execution-complete until both are green — fix failures and re-run rather than skipping or disabling checks. When you transition, paste the full test/lint run output (or a summary with pass counts and zero failures) into the transition comment as proof the tests-green gate was satisfied. If you cannot get them green after reasonable effort, transition to execution-failed with the error output in the comment instead.

Verify the build against the intake's stated acceptance criteria, item by item. For each criterion: state whether it is met, partially met, or not met, and why. This is a mechanical checklist pass, not a judgment call on code quality or architecture (those are separate gates). Emit blocking findings and transition to acceptance-fix if any criterion is not met; otherwise transition to code-quality-review.
Address every blocking finding from the acceptance-criteria review. When done, transition back to acceptance-review so it can re-verify.

Review the implementation for code quality: readability, that tests exist and are passing, error handling, and no slop or dead code. Emit blocking findings and transition to code-quality-fix if anything blocks; otherwise transition to architecture-review.
Address every blocking finding from the code-quality review. When done, transition back to code-quality-review so it can re-verify.

Review the implementation's structure: module boundaries, whether abstractions match the actual need (not over- or under-engineered), and scalability of the approach. Emit blocking findings and transition to architecture-fix if anything blocks; otherwise transition to ux-review.
Address every blocking finding from the architecture review. When done, transition back to architecture-review so it can re-verify.

Review the UI/flows/states/accessibility against the intake by reading the code (components, routes, templates) — this is a code-level heuristic review, not a live run of the app; actually driving the running app through a browser is a later follow-up, not part of this gate. Check for: missing loading/error/empty states, obvious accessibility gaps (labels, alt text, keyboard nav), and flows that don't match what the intake described. Emit blocking findings and transition to ux-fix if anything blocks; otherwise transition to final-review.
Address every blocking finding from the UX review. When done, transition back to ux-review so it can re-verify.

promptOverrides.triage: This is a NEW web application being built from scratch. Use the intake answers (stack, auth, persistence, deploy target, non-goals, acceptance criteria) to write a tight spec. Default to the requested stack; if unspecified, prefer a boring, well-supported stack (e.g. TypeScript + a mainstream framework) over anything exotic.
promptOverrides.planner: Plan the scaffold: project structure, framework choice, routing, auth integration, persistence layer, and deploy target, in that order. Call out the minimum viable slice that satisfies the acceptance criteria — do not plan speculative features beyond the stated non-goals boundary.
promptOverrides.implementer: Scaffold the new application. Prefer official CLIs/starters over hand-rolled boilerplate. Wire up auth and persistence only to the extent the intake requires; leave clear TODOs for anything explicitly out of scope.

intakeQuestions.label: What are you building? Give a one-paragraph description.
intakeQuestions.placeholder: e.g. A customer-facing dashboard for viewing order history.

intakeQuestions.label: Preferred tech stack (language, framework, major libraries)?
Authentication requirements, if any?
intakeQuestions.placeholder: e.g. Email/password via Auth0, or none for MVP

intakeQuestions.label: Data persistence needs?
intakeQuestions.placeholder: e.g. PostgreSQL via Prisma, or none

intakeQuestions.label: Where will this be deployed?
intakeQuestions.placeholder: e.g. Vercel, internal k8s cluster, not yet decided

intakeQuestions.label: What is explicitly out of scope for this work?
intakeQuestions.placeholder: e.g. Mobile app, admin panel, billing

intakeQuestions.label: How will you know this is done? List concrete acceptance criteria.
intakeQuestions.placeholder: e.g. User can sign up, log in, and see their order history
